races.name: Oktoberfest 3rd And 10th October Maiden Fillies' Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Estupenda
runners_data.note: Long absence (124 days) is the headline concern for this prominent-style filly whose sole run was a fifth on Standard AW going; Joey Ramsden's 0/4 14-day record suggests she is not in peak form.

runners_data.name: Kokumi
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and style unconfirmed, with two runner-up finishes on Good ground; Gina Mangan takes over for a yard without recent course winners — modest expectations warranted until she shows her hand here.

runners_data.name: Quiet Soul
runners_data.note: Sean Levey a significant booking for Michael Herrington's hold-up filly, who has already finished second on Standard AW going and third at 5f; the 45-day break is manageable and a strong pace plays directly into her late-running profile.

runners_data.name: Sayidah Dubawi
runners_data.note: Debut runner for James Tate who operates at 4/18 in 14-day returns, with Billy Loughnane a high-quality pilot — going preference and style are entirely unknown, which makes her hard to place but a strong market move would command respect.

runners_data.name: Sioux Moon
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes hold-up filly who was third at 6f on Good going last time; stepping back to 5f here suits a horse who should be produced late, and the pressured pace is precisely what she needs to close into.

runners_data.name: Viking Barbie
runners_data.note: Has run five times and shown consistent form at 5f, including on Standard AW, but wins have not come — Marco Ghiani must decide early whether to fight for the lead or concede and pop the question from slightly off the pace.

runners_data.name: Beautiful Effort
runners_data.note: Has her best form on Standard AW surface (2nd at 5f), and Silvestre De Sousa is an astute booking; a prominent runner by nature, she will need to find a clean position quickly given three confirmed front-runners likely to fill the early slots.

runners_data.name: Chiwara
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's hold-up filly was second at 6f on Good last time and arrives 60 days fresh; Barry McHugh keeps the ride and dropping to 5f is a slight query, but a truly run race on a flat track could allow her class to surface late.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Mystery
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's front-runner has form at both 5f on Good and form over the course trip; a unseat in recent history is a minor flag, but Luke Morris on a confirmed leader at Southwell Flat in a pace-contentious race is the most interesting tactical angle of the race.

races.paceDynamic: Delightfully Hot, Viking Barbie, and Cosmic Mystery are all confirmed front-runners who will contest hard for the early lead over this 5f Southwell flat sprint, guaranteeing a strong, pressured gallop from the outset. With three horses fighting for the same real estate down the stands rail, sectionals are likely to be fast early and the pace will not ease — any of the three could crack under self-inflicted pressure, or collectively drag the field through in a time that tests raw stamina rather than tactical speed. The prominent runners Beautiful Effort and Estupenda sit just off the boil but will themselves be under pressure to find a position in a compressed early order. This race shape — contested pace, honest gallop, no let-up — classically favours hold-up or midfield horses who can travel with cover and pick up the pieces in the final furlong, making Quiet Soul, Sioux Moon, and Chiwara the profiles best suited to the way this race will unfold.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out by halfway, leaving the closer brigade to sweep past the exhausted leaders.
scenarios.body: Delightfully Hot, Viking Barbie, and Cosmic Mystery set a fierce pace that collapses their individual chances inside the final furlong, opening the door for hold-up types tracking in behind. Quiet Soul, Sioux Moon, and Chiwara — all comfortable coming off a strong pace — are the profiles most likely to benefit from the carnage up front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front trio — most likely Cosmic Mystery — establishes a clear advantage at the break and controls the tempo without a prolonged early duel.
scenarios.body: A single leader dictating pace on a flat, fair surface at Southwell can be very hard to peg back over 5f if the opposition spends energy scrapping behind rather than closing. Cosmic Mystery, with Archie Watson's record and Luke Morris's tactical awareness, is best placed to exploit this if Viking Barbie or Delightfully Hot miss the break or are outpaced away.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutante Class Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Sayidah Dubawi or one of the lightly raced OR=120 debutantes has the raw talent to overcome tactical disadvantage and run past a pace-honest field.
scenarios.body: A maiden filly with a high ceiling OR and a top jockey (Billy Loughnane aboard Sayidah Dubawi) can exploit a truly run race if she is well enough educated at home to produce a smooth run from an unknown style position. Chiwara, who finished second at Goodwood, similarly arrives with class in hand relative to her rivals and could pick off a tiring field from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace battle resolves quickly with one leader kicking clear and a prominent racer Beautiful Effort or Estupenda latches onto their heels and outstays them.
scenarios.body: In a race where the front runners burn pace but one survives, a horse sitting second or third and travelling smoothly could edge past a tiring leader without needing a big finishing kick. Beautiful Effort's course form on Standard AW ground (2/5f/STA) gives her a slim but genuine each-way claim in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Cosmic Mystery, Delightfully Hot, and Viking Barbie — watch the first furlong closely; if all three go hammer and tongs for the lead, sectional fractions will be extreme and the race could be effectively over for the entire front three before halfway.

Sayidah Dubawi — an unraced Billy Loughnane-ridden filly for James Tate on debut; any market support in the final 30 minutes before post time should be treated as informed money and warrants attention disproportionate to her unknown profile.

Quiet Soul — Sean Levey is a clear upgrade in riding quality for this hold-up filly; if she gets cover early and the pace collapses as expected, she is the runner most naturally positioned to benefit from the race shape.

Estupenda — 124 days off the track for Joey Ramsden, who has not had a recent Flat winner in the 14-day window; if she shows any signs of race-rustiness in the market or parade ring, she can be dismissed with confidence despite the eye-catching OR=120.

races.review_reason: style/note conflict — check before trusting notes

races.name: Book The Bistro In Seasons Restaurant Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Edwardtheninth
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 1m6f Southwell trip on Standard 64 days ago and holds strong similar-going credentials (1W5P in 14 runs); though its natural instinct is to come from the rear, redistribution means it maps ahead of its preferred position, which tempers confidence in a late burst if the pace doesn't genuinely collapse.

runners_data.name: Lednikov
runners_data.note: Trainer Ivan Furtado has a strong 14-day record here (0/12 strikes counted, but active string), and this veteran eight-year-old wants further than 1m2-1m4f judged on recent history — today's 1m6f is a positive; wears a hood and arrives 16 days fresh, but its true hold-up style is compromised by the single-file pace scenario placing it closer than ideal.

runners_data.name: Blue Tulip
runners_data.note: Three-year-old wearing a hood, trained by the Muir & Grassick operation currently firing at 2/15 in the 14-day window; the step back to 1m6f after failing to stay further is logical, and a win over 1m2f on Standard last month gives confidence about the surface — a genuine hold-up profile that needs something to run at late on.

runners_data.name: Sound Gloria
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's lightly-raced filly has won at 1m2f on Good and placed over 1m4f Good, so the step to 1m6f on Fibresand is the key question; her prominent style is perfectly suited to tracking Be Hopeful and pouncing, and Varian's operation (5/17 in 14 days) is functioning well.

runners_data.name: Be Hopeful
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's three-year-old is the confirmed lone pace-setter and has Sean Levey booked for what looks a straightforward lead; form figures of 7-0-6 are modest but on Standard going at Southwell the conditions are familiar, and dictating without pressure is a substantial positional advantage over 1m6f.

runners_data.name: Le Rouge Chinois
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the ride on a horse carrying 140lbs after two consecutive placed efforts over 1m4-1m6f on Standard — the course and distance profile (0W, 4P from 10 runs on similar going) tells of consistency without a win; wears a hood and the extended trip is a positive.

runners_data.name: Tropical Talent
runners_data.note: Returning from a 451-day absence for the Greenall & Guerriero yard after a series of placed efforts over 1m6-1m7f on Good — the switch to Fibresand is unproven and the fitness question after over a year off is unavoidable; wears a tongue-tie and prominent style suits the anticipated pace shape if fit.

races.paceDynamic: Be Hopeful is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival looking to dispute the lead, will control the fractions from the outset over this 1m6f Fibresand trip at Southwell — Standard conditions suit a horse that sets a measured, sustainable gallop rather than a pressured one. Sound Gloria and Tropical Talent will press from a prominent position just off the leader, providing enough company to keep the pace honest without turning it into a true test of stamina. Le Rouge Chinois, Blue Tulip, Edwardtheninth and Lednikov complete the field, with the latter two redistributed to midfield on the pace map despite being natural hold-up types — the field actually carries more rear-end horses than the map can accommodate at the back, meaning Edwardtheninth and Lednikov are the runners least likely to secure their preferred position. With a lone leader dictating a controlled gallop and a moderate overall tempo, this race shape heavily favours prominent racers who can track the pace and produce a decisive move around the home turn rather than horses depending on a late sectional collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Be Hopeful Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Be Hopeful crosses and dictates without serious challenge, setting a comfortable single-file gallop that rewards the prominent profile.
scenarios.body: Sean Levey slots Be Hopeful into an uncontested lead and controls the tempo throughout, with the prominent duo of Sound Gloria and Tropical Talent close enough to capitalise should the leader tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Sound Gloria or Tropical Talent build enough momentum off a slowing pace to sweep past Be Hopeful inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A modest gallop set by Be Hopeful compresses the field into a sprint finish, and the prominent horses positioned just behind inherit the race without needing significant acceleration.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically in the home straight and Le Rouge Chinois or Blue Tulip produce a sustained finish from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Le Rouge Chinois, who has shown consistent placed form at this trip on Standard, closes powerfully if a genuine pace collapse opens a gap; Blue Tulip is three years old and may benefit from the step back up in trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Breaks Up Field
scenarios.trigger: If Tropical Talent's 451-day absence or Be Hopeful's lack of win form unravels the anticipated race order.
scenarios.body: With the anticipated pace picture in disarray, Edwardtheninth or Lednikov — mapped to midfield but naturally further back — find themselves advantageously placed relative to expectations and benefit from a scrambled finish.

watchPoints.text: Be Hopeful (Sean Levey) — monitor the early splits; if the lead is uncontested through the first half-mile, the controlled tempo could allow the leader to steal a decisive advantage that the hold-up horses cannot peg back.

Tropical Talent — 451 days off the track is a significant fitness concern; if it shows signs of greenness or labours after the home turn, Sound Gloria is best placed to inherit a clear-run victory having tracked throughout.

Le Rouge Chinois — top weight of 140lbs over 1m6f is the heaviest burden in this field; watch whether De Sousa rides prominently rather than holding up, as any deviation from a true hold-up run would change its finishing prospects materially.

Edwardtheninth and Lednikov — both are genuine last-to-first horses placed ahead of their comfort zone by the race shape; if either gets shuffled back to the rear naturally in running, watch for a closing run only if Be Hopeful ties up inside the final two furlongs.

Blue Tulip (Billy Loughnane) — hood first-time or continuing; watch for how settled she is in the early stages, as a three-year-old filly on Fibresand over 1m6f could be outpaced if the field moves forward quickly from the gates.

races.name: Winter Ladies Evening Sat 28th November Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Faeberon
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Standard at Southwell last time — the most directly relevant piece of form in the field; races prominently under Jack Mitchell and the Crisford yard are in fair shape over 14 days; the 1m3f trip is an untested extension but the style and course-form combination makes this a serious contender.

runners_data.name: Saxophonist
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type with consistent placed form on Good ground but no wins; the switch to Standard Fibresand is the key uncertainty, and Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim helps offset the weight; needs the race to be truly run to get involved from the rear.

runners_data.name: New Bay Star
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in this field and likely to have things all her own way from the front; Michael Appleby's yard has been quiet over 14 days and she hasn't won on Standard going in her recent runs, but her control of the race shape makes her the pivotal horse tactically regardless of outcome.

runners_data.name: Golspie
runners_data.note: Solid Southwell Standard form with 12 runs on the surface — the most course-experienced horse in the field; Patrick Morris's runner is a natural hold-up type but the weight of similar horses means he is unlikely to get to the back of the field as intended, which slightly undermines his finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Pace Attack
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's 3-year-old has been kept busy and steps up in trip having run exclusively at 8f-12f on Standard; a true hold-up type by style but is shown in midfield on the map because the field is over-stocked with closers, which means racing closer than ideal and possibly never getting into a rhythm that delivers his best.

runners_data.name: Carwyn
runners_data.note: Consistent tail-ender in recent form with finishing positions of 8,9,9,9,12 — the fade-in-finish flag is well-earned; another Patrick Morris runner alongside Golspie, and a natural hold-up horse forced toward midfield by the race shape, making a winning performance extremely unlikely unless conditions change dramatically.

runners_data.name: Everyoneknowsadave
runners_data.note: The highest-rated horse in the field at OR 75 with a recent Goodwood win over 10f and three placed efforts; races prominently which suits this pace shape, and Liam Wright's 3lb claim keeps the weight competitive — the combination of form, style and rating makes this a prime contender in most scenarios.

runners_data.name: Bearwith
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old who has won twice on Standard going and twice over 10f, making the distance extension to 1m3f the one question; Tom Kiely-Marshall's 5lb claim helps, and the horse's consistency (2W4P on Standard) means it cannot be ignored even though it tends to come from behind in a race that may not set up for closers.

races.paceDynamic: New Bay Star is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the outside, should secure a comfortable lead through the early stages of this 1m3f Southwell flat at a tempo she controls entirely. Faeberon and Everyoneknowsadave are the most likely prominent challengers, sitting just off the pace and providing a degree of attendance without generating genuine pressure on the leader. The hold-up brigade — Saxophonist, Bearwith, Golspie, Pace Attack and Carwyn — are numerous, and with three of those (Golspie, Pace Attack, Carwyn) redistributed to midfield on the map because the field simply cannot accommodate that many genuine back-markers, the race shape is likely to compress into a middle-ground procession rather than a true front-and-back split. A controlled, single-lead race on standard Fibresand at Southwell overwhelmingly favours horses travelling prominently or close to the pace, as the leader sets a metronomic rhythm, the closer ground never gets truly testing, and genuine hold-up horses rarely generate the finishing surge needed to close down a horse who has dictated throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: New Bay Star Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If New Bay Star secures the lead uncontested and sets a sustainable gallop that suits prominent trackers over closers.
scenarios.body: New Bay Star bowls along in front at a steady Standard-going clip, with Faeberon and Everyoneknowsadave locked into position just behind; when the tempo lifts from two furlongs out the horses who have travelled comfortably in the first three are best placed to respond.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If New Bay Star fades inside the final two furlongs after dictating, leaving Faeberon or Everyoneknowsadave to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: A steady early gallop set by New Bay Star flatters the pace but she ties up approaching the final bend, handing the initiative to the two prominent types travelling fluidly just behind; Everyoneknowsadave's recent win form and Faeberon's Southwell Standard-going placed effort make both live dangers in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Get Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough early to string the field out and leave a genuine gap for hold-up horses to exploit in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Saxophonist and Bearwith, both with winning form at Standard Southwell trips, would need the fractions in the first half-mile to be genuinely strong to bring them into play; Bearwith has two wins on Standard-going and Saxophonist has consistent placed efforts, so a rare pace collapse at the front could see one of them finish powerfully.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compression Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely mid-race turning it into a messy sprint finish from a bunched field.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up types redistributed toward midfield the field is liable to bunch, and a messy sprint suits a horse with a high cruising speed already engaged at pace; Everyoneknowsadave's consistent form figures and Faeberon's versatility give them the edge if it degenerates into a flat-out dash from two furlongs out.

watchPoints.text: New Bay Star's ability to control the tempo entirely unchallenged is the hinge of this race — if she gets a soft lead her pace and position could be enough to hold on, but watch whether Faeberon or Everyoneknowsadave push up aggressively in the first two furlongs.

Golspie and Carwyn are both Patrick Morris runners who are natural hold-up types competing in a race where the back of the field is over-subscribed — watch for interference or traffic issues in the final three furlongs if the field compresses.

Pace Attack is trained by Sir Mark Prescott, whose horses have a strong record of peaking fresh and on specific going — with only 14 days since the last run and a step up in trip, monitor whether this runner settles in a midfield position it is not ideally suited to.

Everyoneknowsadave carries the highest weight in the field at 142lbs with the 3lb claim from Liam Wright — in a compressed race shape any weight-carrying disadvantage in the final furlong could be decisive, particularly if New Bay Star has already set a strong pace into the home straight.

Saxophonist has not raced on Standard Fibresand in any of its five recent runs, all on Good ground — the going switch is the biggest unknown for this runner and its hold-up style means it will be among the last to find out if Standard suits it.

races.name: Festive Fixtures At Southwell Racecourse Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Portman Blue
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with solid Standard-going form across sprint-to-mile trips, but six consecutive placed-or-beaten runs (best recent effort a 4th at 8f Standard) suggest a horse that gets into the mix without converting; 32 days off, Luke Morris takes the ride.

runners_data.name: Izzari
runners_data.note: Andrew Mullen partners this 5yo who recorded a course-winning second at Good over 8f and has solid similar-going credentials (1W1P from 5 comparable runs); drops back from longer trips recently and needs a proper gallop to deliver his best from hold-up.

runners_data.name: Peaceful Spirit
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4yo with only three similar-going runs to assess, all finishes of 4th-6th suggesting mid-division consistency without the upside; Alistair Rawlinson rides for a trainer who has had no winners in the last 14 days (0/8), which tempers confidence here.

runners_data.name: Aspull
runners_data.note: Phil McEntee's 4yo is a natural hold-up horse in terms of his running style, yet his form over this trip on good ground is modest; racing only 9 days after his last run and with just one similar-going run to reference, he is likely to settle off the pace rather than press for the early spot the map suggests.

runners_data.name: Just Typical
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane takes over on this 5yo prominent racer who has placed three times at this trip including a win, and whose Standard-going record (1W3P from 8 similar runs) is the best among the prominent brigade; 25 days since last run and a clean bill on going are positives.

runners_data.name: Avatar Jet
runners_data.note: A genuine each-way candidate: Zak Wheatley's mount won at 8f Standard most recently and has three Standard-going places to back that up, and racing from a hold-up position into a potentially compressed midfield suits his style if the pace hotting up opens a gap late.

runners_data.name: Volto di Medusa
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner who carries a [STYLE_FIT=0.93] flag suggesting he may not fully confirm at his natural speed; Cieren Fallon's tactical nous matters here, and while the horse has won twice at this course and trip, his 12 career similar-going runs for 2W5P indicate rivals often reel him in.

runners_data.name: Relevant Range
runners_data.note: Elle-May Croot (5lb claim) partners this 7yo prominent type who has an excellent similar-going record (2W6P from 10 runs) and won at 8f on Good ground; the claim is useful at the weights but the modest recent form (best a 1st seven runs ago) is a note of caution.

runners_data.name: Rusheen Boy
runners_data.note: Sean Levey on a 5yo who has run two seconds and two wins at this sort of trip, though mostly on Good or Soft going — his Standard-going record (2W2P from 6 runs) is respectable; returned 34 days off and carries blinkers, which could sharpen his prominent-style racing.

runners_data.name: Soames Forsyte
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves rides this 7yo whose natural running style is hold-up, placed in the midfield here because the rear is oversubscribed; a [STYLE_FIT=0.91] discount applies, and while he has placed form at 8f Standard, his recent finishing positions (5-5-10-5-5) point to a horse that gets into the race without threatening at the top.

runners_data.name: Bajan Bandit
runners_data.note: Paddy Bradley's 6yo has placed six times from 12 Standard-going runs without winning, with two seconds at this trip specifically; wears a visor and races prominently, giving him a positional edge, but the absence of a win in this profile is telling.

runners_data.name: Special Breeze
runners_data.note: 103 days off is a significant flag for this 4yo, whose natural hold-up style has been redistributed to midfield — she is unlikely to stride forward naturally and the layoff combined with a [STYLE_FIT=0.90] discount makes this a speculative proposition at best; Pam Sly's 1/3 trainer record in the past 14 days offers minimal confidence.

runners_data.name: Aim For The Bull
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby's 4yo has won three of his last five runs including two at 8f Standard, and his similar-going strike rate (2W4P from 12 runs) is among the best in the field; prominent style suits the predicted race shape and 63 days off is the only query, though he wore a visor in his placed run at this trip.

runners_data.name: Mr Fustic
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani rides an 8yo who has an outstanding similar-going profile (2W5P from 14 runs) and won at 8f Standard; his true hold-up style means he is mapped to midfield due to field congestion rather than by inclination — a [STYLE_FIT=0.92] discount applies — but his sheer consistency at this track and going keeps him in the frame if the race develops a proper searching gallop.

races.paceDynamic: Volto di Medusa is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, Cieren Fallon will be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on the Fibresand mile at Southwell. Just Typical, Rusheen Boy, Relevant Range, Bajan Bandit and Aim For The Bull all carry prominent-running profiles and will jostle for the first few positions behind the leader, creating a compact early order rather than a true pace war. The field contains a glut of hold-up horses — Aspull, Soames Forsyte, Special Breeze and Mr Fustic are all natural hold-up types who have been redistributed into the midfield on the map because the rear is already congested; in reality they will be ridden to settle in the back half of the pack, meaning the true closers are numerous and will be fighting for the same ground late. A single, uncontested front-runner controlling a fair but not scorching pace on a flat AW mile favours horses racing prominently just off the leader — those who can track Volto di Medusa without burning their petrol and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out will hold the positional edge over the genuine closers, who face a traffic puzzle and a tempo that may not generate enough late pace to mow them down.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Volto Controls, Prominent Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Volto di Medusa leads unchallenged and sets a fair but unspectacular tempo, allowing the horses tracking just behind to conserve energy and strike from two out.
scenarios.body: The race unfolds at a steady-to-fair clip with Volto di Medusa dictating, and the prominent holders — Just Typical, Rusheen Boy and Aim For The Bull — race within striking distance before unleashing sustained runs that the back-markers cannot match.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Volto di Medusa finds an uncontested lead at a genuinely moderate tempo and Fallon conserves enough to simply stay on stronger than everything else.
scenarios.body: With no challenger to the lead and a slow first half, Volto di Medusa builds an unassailable advantage and the closers' finishing kicks are blunted by ground already conceded; the horse's decent record at this course and trip (2W at 8f Standard) supports this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Cut Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners push the pace harder than expected and the gallop becomes testing enough for genuine hold-up horses to finish through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: A genuinely honest pace would compromise the energy reserves of the prominent brigade, opening the door for Avatar Jet or Izzari to pick up late; Avatar Jet's recent 1st at 8f Standard and Izzari's second at Good over this trip make them the most credible beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinders Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a muddling, uneven pace that creates a bunched midfield and advantages horses who can travel smoothly through the pack.
scenarios.body: In a stop-start gallop, redistributed hold-up types such as Mr Fustic and Soames Forsyte — both of whom have course-and-distance form — could creep into contention, though their out-of-role positioning on the map and lower style-fit scores temper this scenario's likelihood materially.

watchPoints.text: Volto di Medusa (Fallon) — if he gets a completely uncontested lead from the break and the pack allows him to dictate a slow first half, the field may leave him too much room to extend and be uncoordinated in their challenge.

Just Typical and Aim For The Bull — both prominent racers with strong Standard-going records who will try to press Volto di Medusa; if they both push forward aggressively it could compress the early pace and shift the scenario toward a closer's finish.

Avatar Jet — watch whether Zak Wheatley can find clear daylight from a hold-up position; if he gets a clean run from two furlongs out his recent 8f Standard win makes him a live threat to the prominent brigade in Scenario C.

Mr Fustic — 104 days off the track for this 8yo who has excellent course-and-distance form; fitness on return is the key unknown, and if Andi Brown has him race-ready he could outrun his odds from a midfield position despite the redistribution caveat.
Special Breeze — 103 days absent alongside a [STYLE_FIT=0.90] redistribution flag; monitor market moves for any indication of stable confidence, otherwise treat as a non-factor in the pace map.

races.name: Southwell Racecourse Conference & Events Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Mayflower Billy
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up operator for Jessica Macey who has not run for 60 days and has zero wins or places in six outings at similar going; without a strong pace to chase into, finding the winner from the back will be extremely difficult here.

runners_data.name: Silky Lass
runners_data.note: Alex Jary (3lb claim) picks up the ride for Joey Ramsden and this 3yo filly boasts the best Southwell AW record in the field with 1 win and 6 places from 10 attempts at similar going — a clear Fibresand specialist who is effective racing prominently and will be searching for that form fresh off 64 days off.

runners_data.name: Power Strike
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho runner returning after a long 144-day absence, which is the longest layoff in this field, and has only three career runs to her name; she races prominently and handles Southwell AW (one start), but the lack of recent work is a notable query.

runners_data.name: Wield
runners_data.note: Luke Morris booked for Joseph Parr's gelding, who was last seen just 11 days ago and carries the headgear note (t=tongue tie); he is a hold-up type whose Southwell form (sim-going 0W1P) is modest, and a slowly-run race controlled by Filly Eilish will work firmly against him.

runners_data.name: Filly Eilish
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's filly is the race-shaper — De Sousa takes over and she has solid Southwell AW credentials (1W3P in sim-going) but carries a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93, meaning she is classified here as racing out of her most natural role, so discount slightly if the tactical picture shifts and she is pressured off her stride.

runners_data.name: Legacy Rock
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane rides this hold-up type who was also out just 11 days ago; the gelding has a strong record on good ground but has zero wins and no places from three Southwell attempts (sim-going 0W0P), and racing from the back against a lone front-runner who controls pace is an unfavourable setup.

runners_data.name: Test Run
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's runner is a genuine hold-up horse in natural style but is mapped to midfield in this shape because the field cannot accommodate so many rear-runners; Shay Farmer (5lb claim) takes the ride, form is modest (three runs, best is 4th), and the tactical disadvantage of not getting a true position is a real concern.

runners_data.name: Dacres Cross
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's gelding has shown consistent form over shorter trips on good ground — all five career runs have been at 6f-7f on good or soft, so today's 1m on Fibresand is an unproven step in both trip and surface; a natural hold-up horse whose mapping into midfield understates the positional challenge it faces in this shape.

runners_data.name: Vega Storm
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey yard in good form (T14: 7/47), but Vega Storm is a hold-up type displaced toward midfield by the field's structure, and the horse's only Southwell attempt produced a win (sim-going 0W1P is misleading — that's one run with one place); Harry Russell rides, and the AW surface at least is not a complete unknown, though the race shape does not suit its natural running style.

runners_data.name: Sailor's Return
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's hold-up horse ran 28 days ago and shows a tongue-tie in headgear; Cieren Fallon rides but Sailor's Return has zero wins and zero places in three Southwell starts (sim-going 0W0P) and, shifted forward from its natural rear position by the field's density of hold-up runners, the horse is asked to race in an unfamiliar role on an unfavourable surface record.

races.paceDynamic: Filly Eilish is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Silvestre De Sousa can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop around Southwell's flat Fibresand circuit. The field is deceptively hold-up heavy — Test Run, Dacres Cross, Vega Storm and Sailor's Return are all natural rear-runners who have been redistributed into midfield positions on the map because they simply cannot all settle where they want to be, and one or two may push forward and apply modest pressure on Filly Eilish rather than sit deep. That said, with only Power Strike and Silky Lass as natural prominent types alongside her, Filly Eilish is unlikely to face a true pace war and should find a rhythm inside her own comfort zone. This race shape — a single, uncontested pace-setter controlling a mile at standard Fibresand conditions — heavily favours prominent-to-leading profiles and horses with a proven record at this venue, penalising genuine hold-up horses who will find the tempo insufficient to string out the field and create the late gap they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Filly Eilish Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Filly Eilish secures the lead uncontested and De Sousa dictates a steady-to-honest gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Filly Eilish sets her own fractions and, with no rival willing or able to push past her in the early stages, she controls the race from the front and has enough in reserve to kick again entering the straight; her Southwell form (1W3P in sim-going) confirms she handles the surface well and is dangerous when allowed to roll along freely.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Trade Blows
scenarios.trigger: If Power Strike or Silky Lass press Filly Eilish into a contested pace, creating a truly run race from the front.
scenarios.body: A more genuinely run race stretches the hold-up horses wider and suits the horse with the best staying power among the leaders; Silky Lass has the strongest Southwell AW record (1W6P in sim-going) of any runner here and would benefit most if the pace is honest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and produces a truly falsely-run race, allowing one of the deeper-tracked horses to pounce.
scenarios.body: Wield, who has placed at Southwell (sim-going 0W1P) and is fresh off an 11-day turnaround with Luke Morris booked, is the most likely beneficiary among the hold-up types, though even he faces a difficult task generating momentum off a slow early tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stops, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Filly Eilish sets too brisk a pace and ties up in the final furlong, triggering a scramble among multiple challengers.
scenarios.body: An unlikely scenario given the lack of pace rivals and De Sousa's experience in controlling such races, but if the fractions go wrong the field is so closely rated (OR 61–70) that almost any prominent or midfield horse could grab a share; Silky Lass and Power Strike, already in range, are best-placed to profit from a front-runner's collapse.

watchPoints.text: Silky Lass is the biggest danger to Filly Eilish — if Alex Jary uses her natural prominence to sit a close second and stalk the leader through the race, she has the Southwell AW record to back up a challenge in the final furlong.

Power Strike's 144-day absence is the longest in the field and the form book is thin (three runs, none on Fibresand); monitor in the market — if she drifts, the layoff is telling, but if supported she could bounce fresh.

Test Run, Dacres Cross, Vega Storm and Sailor's Return are all natural hold-up horses forced into positions closer to the pace than they would want — watch the early stages for any of them refusing to settle and accidentally creating pressure on Filly Eilish that changes the race shape entirely.

Wield and Legacy Rock both ran just 11 days ago — assess their condition in the paddock given the quick turnaround, as either could be ring-rusty or alternatively bright and forward if connections are targeting this race specifically.

races.name: Southwell Racecourse Conference & Events Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Jackabi
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who handles Standard Fibresand (4/7f/STA placings noted) but steps up from 7f to 1m — the extra furlong is unproven for this 3yo; Mark Rimell's stable is 0/6 in the last 14 days, adding a mild flag.

runners_data.name: Wise Crack
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good last time out for Ruth Carr (1/23 T14), but the sim-going record here is thin (2/10, 0W1P); carries hold-up style that may leave Shane Gray too much to do off this uncontested pace.

runners_data.name: Ballybunion
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 6f on Good ground with Michael Bell but just 0W0P on similar going to today; the horse's natural waiting style sits poorly against a field where only one runner will set the fractions, and Callum Shepherd will need traffic to open up.

runners_data.name: Roi de Coeur
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race — course-and-distance winner (1/8f/STA) handled by Marco Ghiani, trained by Marco Botti (3/17 T14); can set his own terms at a controlled gallop and is impossible to ignore as the race's structural fulcrum.

runners_data.name: Taradif
runners_data.note: Sean Levey in the plate for Jessica Macey (1/3 T14) is a notable booking; 3/8f/GOO last placed run is the only meaningful form over this trip and the STA sim-going is modest (3/5, 0W0P), but the highest OR among the chasers gives him credible staying power.

runners_data.name: Boy Named Sioux
runners_data.note: Returned just nine days ago for Fahey's powerful yard (7/47 T14, 1W1P); Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim is useful and the horse should be ridden forward from gate, giving him a real chance of tracking Roi de Coeur if the hold-up pack concedes ground.

runners_data.name: Alkumatic Jo Jo
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa's booking for Ivan Furtado (0/12 T14) is the headline; seven runners over this course-and-distance gives the most relevant experience in the field (7/11 sim-going, 0W3P) but all those efforts ended in placed finishes at best, not wins, and the natural waiting style is a structural disadvantage today.

runners_data.name: Kiani King
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane partners for Hughie Morrison (0/10 T14) after a 35-day break; hg:t (tongue tie) applied, and the best runs came over 6f rather than a mile — the extra distance on a flat, uncontested pace could expose stamina limits.

runners_data.name: Hunterian
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's yard is active (4/38 T14) and Hunterian has placed twice over 8f on Soft; Andrew Mullen takes over after a 45-day freshen-up, and the horse's form profile (6-in-a-row placed/involved) suggests it stays and tries hard — it just needs the pace to quicken enough to bring it into the race from behind.

races.paceDynamic: Roi de Coeur is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press him for the lead, Marco Ghiani can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front across Southwell's flat Fibresand mile. His recent course-and-distance win (1/8f/STA) and respectable sim-going record (4/6, 1W1P) confirm he is entirely at home here, and an uncontested lead at a moderate pace is the default race shape. The bulk of the remainder — Jackabi, Taradif, Boy Named Sioux, Wise Crack, Ballybunion, Alkumatic Jo Jo, Kiani King and Hunterian — are all hold-up types by style, creating a compressed, waiting pack behind a solo pace-setter who will control every yard. This race shape strongly favours Roi de Coeur and any horse with the tactical speed to track him closely, as a steady lead followed by a stamina-sapping home-straight grind rewards those who race prominently rather than those forced wide or very deep from the rear. Note that five runners — Wise Crack, Ballybunion, Alkumatic Jo Jo, Kiani King and Hunterian — are redistributed to midfield on the map because the field contains far more genuine hold-up horses than there are rear positions; those most likely to actually press Roi de Coeur will be Taradif (highest OR in the chasing group) and Boy Named Sioux (quick turnaround, likely to be ridden handily by the apprentice).

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Roi de Coeur Dictates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Roi de Coeur is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and sets a measured, honest gallop on the front end.
scenarios.body: Ghiani controls tempo from flag to finish, the waiting pack fails to bridge a two-length gap at the two-furlong pole, and course-and-distance form gives Roi de Coeur the decisive edge in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sitting second or third wheel tracks Roi de Coeur throughout and delivers a well-timed challenge inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Taradif or Boy Named Sioux, racing just off the steady pace, has the fresh legs to collar the leader when the gallop steadies rather than quickens; both have the handicap mark and jockey firepower to exploit this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Swoop from Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If Roi de Coeur sets a genuinely brisk pace that causes the field to fan wide and string out, leaving a gap for a strong finisher from the pack.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected tempo would drain the leaders and open the door for a horse buried in midfield to sprint through, though the clustered hold-up group must navigate traffic on a track that does not always reward wide runs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Roi de Coeur fades dramatically inside the final two furlongs having over-set the pace, enabling multiple hold-up horses to arrive together.
scenarios.body: This chaotic shape depends on several redistributed horses racing out of their natural role and is the least structurally likely outcome; Hunterian's placed form over course and trip gives him the best residual claim.

watchPoints.text: Roi de Coeur — if he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a comfortable clip, the standard Fibresand surface gives a solo leader a significant structural advantage and he becomes very hard to run down.

Boy Named Sioux — Warren Fentiman (3lb claimer) is likely to ride handy given the horse's quick turnaround and big-yard confidence; watch whether he slots second or third as that is the prime position to strike from in this shape.
Alkumatic Jo Jo — Silvestre De Sousa may attempt to improve earlier than the horse's natural style allows, blurring the hold-up picture and potentially crowding the midfield pack in the straight.

Taradif — Sean Levey's booking for a small stable (1/3 T14) on a horse with limited Standard-going form is worth monitoring in the market; an unexplained move would shift the probability landscape around Scenario B meaningfully.

Hunterian — the 45-day layoff, yard's 4/38 T14 strike rate and a change of jockey to Andrew Mullen means early market moves on this horse before post time could signal a freshened-up runner primed to outrun a big starting price.

races.name: Gents Evening Saturday 24th October Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sole Spirit
runners_data.note: Returning from 354 days off for Bryan Smart with Paul Mulrennan aboard; has won at 6f on Standard AW going and this surface genuinely suits, but fitness from such a long absence is the critical unknown — natural hold-up style means she needs the pace to honestly test those in front.

runners_data.name: Cairdeas
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves partners a hold-up operator for Paul Midgley who has placed twice at 6f on Standard but never won on the surface; 0W0P on similar going and a tendency to find one too good suggests a place at best rather than a win.

runners_data.name: Dicko The Legend
runners_data.note: Liam Bailey runner whose true racing style is hold-up but is pushed into a midfield position here because of the crowded rear; five consecutive placed or mid-pack finishes on Standard AW going show consistency without a win, and racing without a clear run at the back further limits his upside in this shape.

runners_data.name: Hectic
runners_data.note: A genuine late runner for the same Bailey yard, paired with Jack Garritty, who managed one win on Standard AW but whose natural instinct to come from behind is compromised when the field won't open up the gaps needed; tongue-tie worn, has recorded 9th and 3rd on this surface in the last two starts.

runners_data.name: Baba Reza
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's eight-year-old veterans the course well — placed in four of six runs on Standard AW — and races with a hood; despite genuine hold-up tendencies being squeezed into mid-division by the crowded field, his Southwell course record gives him some claim if a gap appears late.

runners_data.name: Jesse Luc
runners_data.note: A horse with the most course exposure of any runner (14 of 15 runs on similar going, 2 wins), wearing a tongue-piece; though naturally a hold-up type, he has a broader positional range that could help when shuffled mid-pack, and his familiarity with Southwell's layout remains a genuine positive.

runners_data.name: Thunderous Love
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby partners Jonathan Portman's five-year-old who has placed twice from two recent runs at 6f on Good ground; wears a hood and races prominently, which is the ideal position to exploit a controlled Marianne Mozart gallop — going concern exists as all his placed form is on Good or better.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Obsessor
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's four-year-old holds placed form on Standard AW at 5f and has placed twice on similar going overall; a natural hold-up racer placed into midfield by the crowded rear, so benefits slightly from not being buried as deep, though winning on this surface requires a step up.

runners_data.name: Classy Clarets
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner in the race on OR 70, in a rich vein of form (four wins in last five starts) for Iain Jardine with Shay Farmer (5lb claim); carries a hood and races prominently, which is exactly the position this pace map rewards — his form is almost entirely at 5f or 7f on Good/Standard so the 6f trip here is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Hierarchy
runners_data.note: Jamie Osborne's seven-year-old carries a tongue-tie and has a deep 12-run record at 6f on Standard AW; William Carver rides a natural hold-up horse, and while the course form is extensive and reassuring, recent finishes of 9th, 6th and 5th suggest he finds the Southwell straight unkind at present.

runners_data.name: Marianne Mozart
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa's booking for Ismail Mohammed's mare is significant; sole front-runner in the race who can dictate without pressure, though three consecutive 5ths on Standard AW at this trip raise questions about whether she can actually convert positional supremacy into victory when asked to quicken.

runners_data.name: Travel Agent
runners_data.note: Sean Levey partners Adam Kirby's four-year-old who holds a strong record of places (3W4P in 9 STA runs) but has not won since dropping back; equipped with sheepskin cheekpieces, a natural hold-up racer who has found the line quickly before — needs the race to be run at a proper clip to get into it.

races.paceDynamic: Marianne Mozart is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 6f handicap on Southwell's AW Fibresand, and with no other genuine pace horse to pressure her, Silvestre De Sousa can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. Classy Clarets and Thunderous Love will press forward into prominent positions, but neither is likely to force a truly searching pace that would fully test the leader. The field behind is dominated by hold-up types — Hectic, Dicko The Legend, Baba Reza, Jesse Luc, Fantasy Obsessor and others — many of whom cannot all occupy their preferred rear position simultaneously and will be shuffled into midfield against their instincts, reducing their effectiveness as closers. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or just off a controlled leader, rather than deep closers relying on a generous pace to pull them through; hold-up horses racing out of role face a genuinely disadvantaged setup.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Marianne Mozart Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Marianne Mozart sets an uncontested, even gallop and the hold-up pack fails to generate the sustained late run the race shape doesn't invite.
scenarios.body: De Sousa rolls along at a comfortable clip, keeping his advantage into the final furlong where the closers are caught in traffic or lack the momentum to peg him back; prominent horses just off the pace inherit the placing positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just quick enough to string out the field and a prominent racer picks up the front-runner inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Classy Clarets, in fine in-form shape and carrying headgear, is ideally placed just off the leader and can pounce with a superior turn of foot; Thunderous Love, recording consecutive placed efforts, benefits from the same position without being exposed to a punishing pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Thread Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens early enough to create gaps in the straight and one of the deeper hold-up horses finds a clear run at a crucial moment.
scenarios.body: Sole Spirit, who has genuine course-and-distance form on this surface and returns from a 354-day absence into a smaller, calmer field, represents the best hold-up profile if she's fit; Hierarchy has course experience and enough tactical versatility to fill the gap.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Hold-Up Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop collapses into a dawdle that produces a sprint finish with no clear separation until the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Fantasy Obsessor and Jesse Luc, both redistributed from their natural rear positions into midfield, find themselves better placed than expected in a messy late sprint; the compressed field negates pedigree and favours whoever gets the clearest daylight.

watchPoints.text: Marianne Mozart is the sole front-runner — watch whether De Sousa controls the gallop or is content to let the pace drift dangerously slow, as an unusually sedate fractions would flip the advantage toward the hold-up pack.

Classy Clarets is top-rated on OR 70 but has achieved all his form at 5f or 7f; watch how Shay Farmer positions him in the first two furlongs — if he settles cleanly off the leader at 6f he is the biggest threat to the pace scenario, but if he over-races early his stamina may be tested.

Several Bailey runners (Hectic, Dicko The Legend) are both hold-up types placed into midfield — watch their draws and early position at the break, as both starting wide or losing early ground will compound their already compromised race shape.

Sole Spirit returns from 354 days off — watch her pre-race appearance and whether Smart declares first-time headgear; if she shows no market support, her fitness should be treated as genuinely uncertain despite the strong surface form.

Jesse Luc's unmatched course experience (14 of 15 runs on this configuration) is worth tracking in-running — if the field bunches entering the final furlong, his route knowledge could give him a fractional positional advantage over rivals less familiar with the track's unique contours.

races.name: Celebrate With Sponsorship At Southwell Racecourse Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Masai Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly from the powerful Fahey yard returning in fair order (23 days); one course-and-distance win from limited similar-going starts but has finished outside the places on both recent Goodwood starts, and as a genuine rear-runner she will need a clean passage in a 14-runner field.

runners_data.name: Rogue Federation
runners_data.note: Carries a fade-in-finish flag and has placed only in 2 of 3 similar-going outings; though shown in midfield on the map, this is a true hold-up horse pushed forward by a crowded rear, meaning a strong pace is needed to bring its finishing effort into play.

runners_data.name: Yes Waliim
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has course form, winning over 7f on Standard; Oliver Hoodless takes a 7lb claim which helps, and this horse has genuine hold-up tendencies that the map shifts forward due to field congestion — its best chance is if the pace burns hot and a gap opens late.

runners_data.name: Based
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon rides a horse who has won over 7f on Standard going and shows a consistent placed record at that trip; a true hold-up performer absorbed into the midfield pack on the map, making its finish dependent on traffic clearing — the drop to 6f from its winning distances is also a mild concern.

runners_data.name: Soul Warrior
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and fades in finish, which is a double concern in a race likely to produce a strong gallop; Alex Jary's 3lb claim is modest compensation, and with limited placed form on comparable going, this is a horse whose redistribution from the rear further undermines its realistic chance.

runners_data.name: Great Success
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has shown a string of mid-pack finishes at this course and on similar going (three 4th-5th placings from recent starts); Kieran O'Neill takes over on a horse whose natural hold-up style is crowded backward on the map, and a weak run of form offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Golden Harvest
runners_data.note: Dougie Costello rides a filly returning after 39 days who placed over 5f here on Standard — her best recent form; stepping back up to 6f is a slight query, and as a genuine hold-up type shown in midfield by necessity, she needs things to go very right from the rear.

runners_data.name: Zonnebloem
runners_data.note: Returning from a lengthy 315-day absence and lightly raced, this Jessica Macey-trained filly has placed over 5f at Southwell and Kempton on Standard; Sean Levey is a useful booking but the long layoff is the dominant factor, and as a hold-up type mapped forward, racing fitness is the overriding unknown.

runners_data.name: Lope Y Linda
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Tim Easterby back quickly (9 days) after a recent run; has no wins from 15 starts on similar going, which is a striking statistic, but as one of only two confirmed pace-setters she will control early fractions and could benefit if Society Charm cannot match her early speed.

runners_data.name: Society Charm
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani rides the second confirmed front-runner, returning after a long 140-day break for Peter Chapple-Hyam with a short form string (3 runs, all unplaced); the absence is a genuine fitness concern, and if she cannot sustain early pace she will simply serve as pace-fodder for those tracking behind.

runners_data.name: Surgeon Commander
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner (OR 60) with a strong win record — three wins from 12 similar-going starts including two 7f Southwell wins; Billy Loughnane rides, the hood is retained, and though a genuine hold-up type at his best, his class edge makes him the most dangerous closer if he can find daylight in a busy field.

runners_data.name: Taaklam
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed prominent racer and ideally positioned for this race shape; wears a hood, has placed in three of his last five (including two here at Southwell on Standard), and Tom Kiely-Marshall's 5lb claim is a small bonus — the tactical advantage of sitting just off a contested lead is significant in a race with only two true pace-setters.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Bay
runners_data.note: Jack Garritty rides a Fahey-trained hold-up type who has placed twice at Southwell on Standard (2nd and 3rd); returning after 42 days, he has the course form to be competitive and as a genuine closer with solid placed figures, represents one of the more credible threats from off the pace if pace is strong.

runners_data.name: Love Alive
runners_data.note: Luke Morris rides a hold-up performer who has placed three times from 13 similar-going starts; recent form is inconsistent (9-6-3-0-3-5) and the drop back to 6f suits having run well over shorter, but in a crowded rear-group with several rivals of similar profile, finding a clear run is the central challenge.

races.paceDynamic: Lope Y Linda and Society Charm are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the gates over this 6f Southwell AW straight track, creating a genuinely contested gallop that is unlikely to collapse into a crawl. With 14 runners and a crowded draw, the pace should be honest rather than suicidal, setting up a race that is run at a consistent clip throughout and will test those who cannot travel within striking distance. That honest, unrelenting tempo on a flat, straight course historically favours prominent racers who can sit just off the lead and pick up when the pace-setters tie each other up — Taaklam is the sole confirmed prominent type and is ideally placed for this shape. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the map can absorb at the rear: Rogue Federation, Yes Waliim, Based, Soul Warrior, Great Success, Golden Harvest, Zonnebloem and others are genuine closers who will compete for ground in mid-to-rear pack, and it is the prominent type — or the horse best able to secure a clean rail position tracking the pace — who profits most from this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Lope Y Linda and Society Charm set an honest, even gallop that strings the field out and leaves Taaklam or a handy type to pounce in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners cancel each other out at a sustainable pace, leaving the prominent racer sitting second or third with a clean run into the straight to pick them off; Taaklam's consistent placed form at Southwell and prominent style make this the most natural beneficiary.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Alone
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters (most likely Lope Y Linda) gets an uncontested or lightly contested lead and controls the fractions.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner dictating terms on a flat, straight track can conserve enough energy to hold on, particularly if the hold-up horses are stuck wide or checked in traffic; Lope Y Linda's recent run of form at short notice and Tim Easterby's strong yard stats give her the edge in a solo-lead scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace burns both front-runners off and the field bunches, allowing a hold-up horse to deliver a late run on a tiring field.
scenarios.body: A strong finish pace from mid-rear could catch a spent front end, but this scenario is structurally compromised here because many of the true closers — Based, Rogue Federation, Soul Warrior — are racing in an overcrowded rear and will need a clear passage that is unlikely in 14 runners; Surgeon Commander's higher RPR and course-and-distance winning form give him the best claims if this shape does materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Too Hot, Mid-Pack Profits
scenarios.trigger: If early fractions are genuinely fast and both front-runners blow up, handing momentum to a horse travelling smoothly in mid-division.
scenarios.body: Horses such as Yes Waliim and Masai Angel, though redistributed from their true hold-up position into a midfield slot on the map, could catch a wall of tiring horses if they find daylight; this scenario depends on both a truly unsustainable gallop and a clean run for horses racing out of their natural role, making it the least reliable shape.

watchPoints.text: Society Charm returns after 140 days for Peter Chapple-Hyam with only three career runs — if she is ring-rusty and ties up in the final furlong rather than pressing Lope Y Linda, the early pace drops and the race shape changes entirely.

Taaklam is the only confirmed prominent horse in a 14-runner field; if he secures a clean rail position tracking the front pair into the final furlong, he is racing in the ideal tactical slot for this shape and should be respected accordingly.

Surgeon Commander (OR 60, three wins) is the highest-rated runner and a three-time Southwell winner, but Billy Loughnane will need to find clear running through what is likely to be a wall of hold-up horses — watch where he is positioned at halfway.

The redistributed hold-up cluster (Rogue Federation, Based, Soul Warrior, Great Success, Golden Harvest, Zonnebloem) creates a serious traffic-jam risk in the rear half of the field; any horse nearest to the rail at halfway gets first run, and those widest out face an impossible task in a 6f straight sprint.

Lope Y Linda's trainer Tim Easterby has a 4/71 14-day strike rate and the horse runs back quickly (9 days); watch for signs in the market that connections believe an early advantage can translate to a win, as there are no other confirmed front-runners capable of matching her if Society Charm fades.
